Subject: Dedicated capacity needs & timeline (AR-928)

Jonas / Sergio —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Acme is planning a phased rollout of our internal analytics assistant tied to AR-928. Our engineering lead asked me to confirm expected capacity lead times so we can finalize go-live dates. High level:
- Expected sustained throughput: ~250 prompt-generations/minute (avg 128 tokens output)
- Peak bursts: ~1.2k req/min for 6–8 minute windows during reporting cycles
- Data residency: US-only

We need options for: (A) Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity with SLA by Oct 15, or (B) a hybrid approach (hosted + burst to cloud OEM). Please let me know realistic procurement lead times for reserved Dedicated (GPU procurement vs cloud reservations), whether you can lock capacity now, and any documents you need from our procurement/legal team.

I attached our capacity worksheet (Acme_AR-928_capacity_request_v2.xlsx).

Best,
Amelia
Head of Product, Acme Analytics

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity needs & timeline (AR-928)

Amelia —

Appreciate the clear worksheet and target dates. Quick summary from our side and initial asks:

1) High-level options and lead times (initial estimate):
   - Reserved Dedicated (Redwood-managed GPU pool / OEM procurement): 10–14 weeks from signed PO for new hardware procurement + setup in Dedicated (sourcing dependent).
   - Cloud reserved capacity (partner clouds like CloudScale): 4–8 weeks to reserve and provision, quicker if we convert existing reserved pools; may require region-specific confirmation for US East.
   - Short-term hybrid (hosted + burst to cloud OEM): immediate hosted capacity, burst reservations within 1–2 weeks for small slot reservations (subject to partner availability).

2) Immediate asks from Acme: please confirm which option you prefer and whether you can share a tentative committed start window (Oct 15 target). Also confirm willingness to execute a limited 3-month commit to reserve capacity (helps prioritize procurement).

3) Internal owners looped: Marissa to advise commercial / pricing; Karthik to confirm model sizing and GPU footprint.

I’ll open conversations with our CloudScale rep and request a preliminary OEM quote.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
VP Sales, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-12T13:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity needs & timeline (AR-928)

Jonas / team —

I pulled the numbers against Acme's worksheet. Technical assumptions and recommended configs:

- Target model family: 70B-class (float16 / bfloat16) with 8k context.
- Sustained throughput target (~250 gen/min) maps to ~2 x A100-40GB-equivalent instances with continuous batching; add 1–2 GPUs for headroom for stateful sessions/KV caches.
- Peak bursts: recommend a small burst pool of 4 GPUs (same family) behind autoscaler to handle 1.2k/min spikes for short windows.

Sizing implication: production Dedicated stack = 4–6 GPUs per cluster for initial rollout. If Acme wants isolation per environment (prod/staging), duplicate capacity or use namespacing with autoscale.

Procurement lead-time guidance (based on recent vendor cycles):
- Direct OEM new GPU orders (ordered through OEM distributor): typically 10–14 weeks after PO; on rare expedite (stock) 6–8 weeks but at premium and availability-dependent.
- Cloud reserved capacity with CloudScale: their US East inventory shows tentative availability in the 6–8 week window for 4–8 GPU reservations; can be faster if we convert existing reserved pools.

Notes / risk: supply can shift quickly. If Acme signs commit this week, we can prioritize requests and get on OEM distributor waitlists which materially shortens lead time when stock arrives. Also recommend we prepare a small hosted-capacity fall-back (1–2 instances) to cover initial launch.

I can draft an ops runbook for onboarding once we pick option.

-Karthik
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

- Pricing: we'll send a preliminary reserved quote (attached stub) showing committed vs on-demand rates.

Attachment: CloudScale_reserve_quote_AR-928.xlsx (note: this is a stub; formal quote will be sent through our sales portal)

Happy to set a short call tomorrow to align timelines and set a reservation hold.

—Alex
